design_decisions.w3_compatibility_block: The DEFINED ac2/ac3 tension (relocate the content AND keep the tokens greppable in README.md) is resolved as a COMPATIBILITY SURFACE rather than a deletion. The prose, rationale and detail move to the three documents; README keeps a compact heading+command surface carrying exactly the tests[128] token set. ac2 fences BOTH sides in one fence - detail present in the new files AND tokens greppable in README - so neither half can regress silently. The surface is temporary by contract: t71 settles the pins and is the only card allowed to remove it.
design_decisions.compat_block_placement: The surface sits BELOW the ## Alternative paths heading, which itself sits after ## Quick Start. That placement is forced, not stylistic: tests[235] (t63 ac4) counts make invocations above the Alternative heading and requires zero, so any make line the compatibility surface carries must sit below it (W2). The measured stub puts Quick Start at line 50 and Alternative at line 130 with zero make invocations in between, and ac3 re-fences that order so a later README card cannot reintroduce make content above the fold.
design_decisions.what_moves_and_what_stays: Moves (mirrored and expanded in the new documents): the Linux/WSL make prose plus test/lint rationale, the two-mode narrative with its compose/migration/secret-rule rationale, the Dashboard API endpoint table detail and verification paragraph, the Screenshots prose and caveats, and expanded copies of the evidence checklist and both five-minute paths. Stays: Features, Prerequisites, Quick Start, Stopping, Troubleshooting, the Dashboard API endpoints heading with its six path tokens, the Alternative heading with its make/test/lint command lines, Local development modes with Mode A / Mode B / Development versus production and their command lines, the Vite dev server and uvicorn --reload sentences, three requirement anchors, Repository layout, the screenshot image reference, the 15-row criteria mapping, the 14-row evidence checklist, both five-minute paths with every step and the honest DEFERRED statement, License, the Render section, and all 60 requirement ids.
design_decisions.why_evidence_and_five_minute_sections_st: DESIGN TENSION STATED PLAINLY: the DEFINED ac3 wording ('README no longer carries the relocated sections') is NOT satisfiable for the Evidence checklist and the two five-minute sections. tests[201] (t49 ac4) reads README.md with sed ranges bounded by top-level headings and requires the criteria-mapping, evidence-checklist, live-verification and local-verification sections with their rows; deleting them to satisfy a literal reading of ac3 would turn a carried gate RED, which this card is forbidden to do. So those three sections STAY in README.md and are additionally mirrored and expanded in docs/verification.md. ac2 fences their survival and ac3 fences the markers that genuinely moved. This is the one place where the card deliberately departs from the stub's literal wording, and it is recorded here rather than hidden.
design_decisions.id_preservation_by_matrix_identity: ac6 does not count requirement ids - counting would pass while a row silently flipped. It REGENERATES the coverage matrix (uv, REQ_COVERAGE_OUT to a temp path) and requires cmp to report BYTE-IDENTICAL against the committed file at 749 rows. That is the exact, falsifiable statement of 'no requirement id lost its last pointer because a section moved', and it was verified byte-identical both at base and on the stub.
design_decisions.pin_rule_fencing: The pin rule is fenced positively rather than by absence. ac6 asserts the stored pin-3 literal still appears EXACTLY ONCE in the byte-frozen index AND that the working README digest has moved off it. Together those two facts prove the delta landed without the pin being edited to match - the failure mode the rule actually guards against. ac5 prints the card-scoped measured attestation (cr-stripped sha256 plus line count) that the verifier confirms against the working bytes. Stored-pin equality is asserted only by t71.
design_decisions.line_ceiling_400: ac5 fences a 400-line ceiling rather than the milestone's 500 so the later v2 cards inherit headroom; the contract-minimal stub measured 343. A 30-line floor is carried alongside so a gutted README fails too.
design_decisions.w4_honest_diff_estimate: The plan estimates 330-400 changed lines against a warn-only max_diff of 300. The contract-minimal delta measured against the conforming stub is 291 lines (README 36 added / 60 deleted = 96, plus 195 lines of new documents). The card reports the estimate AND the measured figure, and ac6 prints a WARN rather than a pass if the builder's version exceeds 300 - the cap is advisory and is not gamed by splitting the card or by deleting content the carried gates need.
design_decisions.windows_worktree_git_reads: Where a fence needs git metadata it does not call git directly: this is a linked worktree whose gitdir holds Windows-formatted paths, so plain git under WSL fails. The fence resolves wslpath -w and pipes cmd.exe /c "git -C <windows-path> ..." with stdin closed (</dev/null), and the delta legs compare the base commit against the WORKING TREE rather than against HEAD so the fence is state-robust (it passes whether or not the builder has committed yet). This is the t65 ac1 lesson: never hand a WSL /mnt/c path to a Windows-side tool, and no fence writes a database or a path outside build/ and the allow-list.

notes: The single most likely way this card misleads a builder: it looks like a deletion card. It is not. Roughly 60 README lines are deleted and 36 are added back as a compatibility surface, because three stored gates (tests[128], tests[201], tests[119]) grep README.md itself for content the DEFINED draft asked to relocate. Deleting the Evidence checklist or either five-minute section to satisfy a literal reading of the draft turns tests[201] RED and fails the card. Read ac2 as the specification of what must remain greppable.

Second trap: the three new documents are NOT citation sources for the coverage matrix, but README.md IS. Moving a requirement id out with its section flips that id's matrix row to GAP. ac6 catches that by regenerating the matrix and requiring byte-identity, so a builder who 'cleanly' moves a section containing the only citation of some id will see ac6 go RED with a cmp failure rather than a doc regression shipping.

Third trap: the CRLF leg in ac5 is not cosmetic. tests[128] uses line-anchored patterns with a trailing [[:space:]], which the CR satisfies. A builder who writes README.md with LF-only working bytes (e.g. by piping through a tool that normalises EOL) keeps a pure-ASCII, correct-content README and still turns tests[128] RED.

ac6 compares the base commit against the WORKING TREE, not against HEAD, so it behaves identically before and after the builder commits. Do not 'fix' it back to a HEAD-to-HEAD diff: that version goes RED on an uncommitted tree and would read as a delta-purity violation.
The screenshot IMAGE reference stays in README.md (the criteria-mapping row that cites it is a carried gate); only the surrounding prose and caveats move to docs/screenshots.md.
